sentences.text: In the present case the claimants are niece and nephew of the deceased Shantavva.
Therefore, the tribunal is correct in not awarding loss of dependency but awarded compensation under the head loss of estate.
But actually it ought to have been under the head loss to estate.
The tribunal has considered income of the deceased at Rs.6,000/- per month and considered 25% of income as loss to estate.
The accident occurred on 03.02.2015.
Therefore, in the absence of proof of income, the notional income would be Rs.8,000/- per month as recognized by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority.

5. In view of the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others, reported in (2017) 16 Supreme Court Cases 680, 10% of the income is to be added towards loss of future prospects in life.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others, reported in (2017) 16 Supreme Court Cases 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 25% of the income is considered as loss to estate.
The deceased was NC: 2023:KHC-D:13459 aged 53 years at the time of accident.
Considering the age of the deceased, appropriate applicable multiplier is 11.
Therefore, compensation towards loss to estate is hereby re-
assessed and quantified as Rs.2,90,400/- (Rs.8,000 + 10% x 25% x 12 x 11).

6. In view of the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co.
Limited v. Nanu Ram & Others, reported in 2018 ACJ 2782 and in the case of Pranay Sethi supra,
the claimants are entitled to Rs.40,000/- each under the head 'loss of consortium', along with 10%
escalation.

sentences.text: Accordingly, Rs.88,000/- (Rs.40,000 x 2 + 10%) is awarded under the head 'loss of consortium including loss of love and affection'.

7. Further, a compensation of Rs.15,000/- is awarded under the head 'funeral and transportation',
along with 10% escalation.
Therefore under this head Rs.16,500/- (Rs.15,000 + 10%) is awarded.

Thus, the claimants would be entitled for compensation under various heads as under:
 Sl. Heads.

Amount in  No. (Rs.)
 1. Towards loss to estate.
3 . Towards transportation of dead 16,500  body & funeral expenses.

Therefore, the claimants are entitled for total compensation of Rs.3,94,900/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of filing of the petition till realization, as against Rs.2,23,000/-
awarded by the tribunal.
The insurance company is directed to deposit the compensation within eight weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.

opennyai_summary.facts:
In the present case the claimants are niece and nephew of the deceased Shantavva.
Therefore, the tribunal is correct in not awarding loss of dependency but awarded compensation under the head loss of estate.

Therefore, in the absence of proof of income, the notional income would be Rs.8,000/- per month as recognized by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority.
25% of the income is considered as loss to estate.
6. In view of the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co.
Limited v. Nanu Ram & Others, reported in 2018 ACJ 2782 and in the case of Pranay Sethi supra,
the claimants are entitled to Rs.40,000/- each under the head 'loss of consortium', along with 10%

7. Further, a compensation of Rs.15,000/- is awarded under the head 'funeral and transportation',

opennyai_summary.decision:
Accordingly, Rs.88,000/- (Rs.40,000 x 2 + 10%) is awarded under the head 'loss of consortium including loss of love and affection'.
Therefore under this head Rs.16,500/- (Rs.15,000 + 10%) is awarded.
Therefore, the claimants are entitled for total compensation of Rs.3,94,900/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of filing of the petition till realization, as against Rs.2,23,000/-
awarded by the tribunal.
The insurance company is directed to deposit the compensation within eight weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
NC: 2023:KHC-D:13459 ORDER i) The appeal in MFA No.102514/2016 filed by the insurance company is dismissed.
ii) The cross objection MFA CROB No.100155/2016 filed by the claimants is allowed in part.
iv) The claimants are entitled for total compensation of Rs.3,94,900/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization, as against Rs.2,23,000/- awarded by the tribunal.
v) The amount in deposit shall be transmitted to the tribunal.
NC: 2023:KHC-D:13459 vi) The insurance company shall deposit the compensation amount within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.
viii) No order as to costs.
